title: The Feature That Nobody Used
summary: Flowboard is a collaborative whiteboard tool for remote teams — teams sketch ideas, run retrospectives, and brainstorm together in real time.

Q1.text: A feature launched six weeks ago — infinite canvas zoom — has near-zero adoption. Only 3% of active teams have tried it. What do you do first?

choices.text: Check whether the feature is discoverable in the UI
choices.reveal: The zoom controls are nested two menus deep — users have to click View, then Canvas, then Zoom. Most never reach it.
choices.because: A feature that's hard to find will look unused even when people want it — discoverability comes first.

choices.text: Survey users who never tried the feature
choices.reveal: Response is mixed — some don't know it exists, some tried and didn't see the point. The survey doesn't separate the two cleanly.

choices.text: Analyze usage patterns of teams that did try zoom
choices.reveal: The 3% who tried it use it heavily — but the sample is too small for conclusions about the other 97%.

choices.text: Deprecate the feature and reallocate engineering time
choices.reveal: The feature is removed — but the discovery problem that hid it from 97% of users goes unaddressed.

Q2.text: The zoom controls are nested two menus deep. What do you do next?

choices.text: Move zoom controls to the primary toolbar and re-measure discovery
choices.reveal: The controls move to the toolbar in a single sprint — the next week, 28% of active teams use zoom, up from 3%.
choices.because: A discoverability fix is cheap and testable — moving the control and measuring the lift confirms the diagnosis.

choices.text: Run a full UX research study on toolbar layout
choices.reveal: The study confirms the zoom controls are buried — but it also surfaces three other navigation issues, muddying the priority.

choices.text: Add an onboarding tooltip for new users explaining zoom
choices.reveal: The tooltip shows for new users — but existing users, who make up most of the active base, never see it.

Q3.text: Survey responses are mixed — some don't know the feature exists, some tried and didn't see the point. What do you do?

choices.text: Segment the responses by whether users found the feature
choices.reveal: 70% of respondents never found the feature in the UI; among the 30% who did, half didn't see the value. Two separate problems.
choices.because: Segmenting the mixed signal separates discoverability from value — each needs a different fix.

choices.text: Conclude the feature has low value and deprioritize it
choices.reveal: The feature is deprioritized — but the 70% who never found it never got the chance to judge its value.

choices.text: Plan a marketing push to promote the feature
choices.reveal: The marketing push runs — but it drives traffic to a feature that's buried two menus deep. Awareness rises, usage doesn't.

Q4.text: The zoom controls are now discoverable, and usage jumped to 28%. But half the users who found it didn't see the value. What do you do?

choices.text: Add an example template that demonstrates a zoom-based workflow
choices.reveal: The template ships with a pre-built brainstorming board at 5 zoom levels — teams using it learn zoom by doing, and 40% keep using it.
choices.because: A template demonstrates value through use — users who experience a zoom workflow understand what it's for.

choices.text: Write better documentation explaining when to use zoom
choices.reveal: The docs improve — but users who didn't see the value don't read docs.

choices.text: Add a feature tour that walks new users through zoom
choices.reveal: The tour shows zoom for new users — but established teams, who are most of the base, skip it.

Q5.text: The template improved adoption. What do you measure to confirm the improvement?

choices.text: Track zoom usage among teams who used the template vs those who didn't
choices.reveal: Template users zoom 3x more in their first week and 40% keep using it after. Non-template users who discover zoom independently show 12% retention.
choices.because: Comparing template users against non-users isolates the template's effect on adoption.

choices.text: Monitor overall platform engagement for the next month
choices.reveal: Overall engagement rises — but without a template-specific segment, you can't isolate the template's contribution from general growth.

choices.text: Count how many teams viewed the template
choices.reveal: View count is high — but views don't correlate with zoom usage. The metric captures curiosity, not adoption.

Q6.text: Template users zoom 3x more and 40% retain. Non-template users who discover zoom independently show 12% retention. What do you do?

choices.text: Add template suggestions to the zoom control when users first open the toolbar
choices.reveal: The suggestion shows when users click the zoom control for the first time — a tooltip with a preview of the brainstorming board at 5 zoom levels. New-user zoom adoption rises 35%.
choices.because: Proactive suggestion at the moment of discovery intercepts users before they abandon zoom.

choices.text: Send an email campaign highlighting the available templates
choices.reveal: The email campaign runs — but users who were already overwhelmed by the UI don't engage with feature emails. Open rates are 4%.

choices.text: Add a video tutorial showing a template-driven workflow
choices.reveal: The video is added — but users scrolling through it see a lot of content they don't need. The video adds complexity rather than reducing it.

Q7.text: The proactive tooltip improved new-user zoom adoption by 35%. But the support team reports that some users complain they can't turn it off. What do you do?

choices.text: Add a 'dismiss' option to the tooltip and track dismissal rate
choices.reveal: The dismiss option is added — dismissal rate is 12%. Those who dismiss don't adopt zoom, which is expected — some users don't want it.
choices.because: A dismiss option respects user choice and the low dismissal rate suggests the tooltip is helpful for most users.

choices.text: Leave the tooltip as-is — it helps most users and dismissals are rare
choices.reveal: The tooltip stays — but the support tickets persist at low volume. The support team flags them as 'feature complaints' in the NPS survey, which drops 2 points.

choices.text: Remove the tooltip — it causes support friction
choices.reveal: The tooltip is removed — but new-user zoom adoption drops back to 24%. The simple UX change was effective for the majority.

Q8.text: The dismiss option is added and new-user zoom adoption stays at 59%. The team asks: is this feature a success now? What do you report?

choices.text: Report adoption (59% new users try zoom) and retention (40% active after template), and identify the remaining 60% as the next opportunity
choices.reveal: The report is clear: 28% of all active teams use zoom (up from 3%), and of those, 40% are retained month-over-month. The remaining opportunity is a simpler onboarding path for the 60% who try once and churn.
choices.because: An honest report that acknowledges both the win and the remaining opportunity gives the team direction for the next iteration.

choices.text: Report the 28% adoption as a major success and close the feature as complete
choices.reveal: The win is celebrated — 28% adoption is a 9x improvement. But the 60% who tried and left represent ongoing churn risk that the team may miss.

choices.text: Celebrate the win and move the team to the next feature request backlog
choices.reveal: The team moves on — but the 60% one-time zoom users are a segment that could be nurtured into regular users with the right follow-up.

criteria.label: Letting evidence lead
criteria.guidance: Name the barrier before judging the feature.

criteria.label: Sizing customer impact
criteria.guidance: Ground the decision in what changes for the user.

criteria.label: Proving the outcome
criteria.guidance: Define the measure that shows the fix worked.
